text:
Fraser Minten is 22 and in his second full season as a Bruin, a big center who came over from Toronto and has settled into 16.5 minutes a night. The numbers on top look like a leap: 7 goals and 13 points in 20 games, a scoring rate of 2.37 points per 60 minutes against 1.65 last season.

Underneath, it is less certain. His 7 goals came on 4.51 expected goals, our measure of the quality of his chances, and his 17.9% shooting is above his usual range of 11.7% to 16.8%. Boston has also scored 7.9 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. Meanwhile the Bruins have taken only 48.5% of 5-on-5 expected goals with him out there, 7.2 points worse than without him. That is scoring built on finishing, not on winning shifts.

The tools are real. His top shot speed sits in the 90th percentile, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 60% of his entries last season. The Sports Hub's Ty Anderson has a suggestion: "I'd put Minten and Pastrnak back together at 5v5." Where Boston plays him is worth watching.
headline: Minten is scoring above his chances in Boston
